value.heading: Cast iron, start to finish.
value.intro: Season it once over fire, cook in it every day, bring it back from anything. Everything we teach in the workshop, in three tabs.

content.heading: Season over fire in four steps

items.title: Scrub it back
items.summary: Hot water and a chainmail scrubber. No soap needed.

image.alt: A chainmail scrubber working over a wet skillet
image.name: chainmail-scrub.jpg

card.title: Start with a bare, dry pan
card.body: Scrub under hot water until the surface feels even, then dry it over the flame for two minutes so no water hides in the pores.

items.title: Oil, then wipe it off
items.summary: The thinnest coat of flaxseed oil you can manage.

image.alt: A lint-free cloth wiping oil from a warm skillet
image.name: flax-wipe.jpg

card.title: Thin coats, every time
card.body: Rub in half a teaspoon, then wipe as if you made a mistake. Thick oil turns sticky instead of hard.

button.label: Why flaxseed
button.title: Seasoning cast iron over an open fire

image.alt: A skillet upside down on the Cable Fold grate above glowing coals
image.name: upside-down-coals.jpg

card.title: Let the fire do the work
card.body: Set the pan face down on the grate over medium coals. Smoke means it's working; keep going until it stops, about 45 minutes.

items.title: Repeat three times
items.summary: Then fry eggs for a week.

card.title: Three coats, then cook
card.body: Three rounds builds a surface that releases an egg on the first try. Daily cooking does the rest.

image.alt: Flaxseed oil, a cloth and a scrubber laid out on a wooden board
image.name: seasoning-kit.jpg

content.heading: Everything for step one
content.body: Oil, cloth and a scrubber in one tin.

content.heading: Already seasoned?
content.body: Every Caldera pan ships with three coats. You can skip straight to the Cooking tab.

card.title: Butter, medium heat, patience
card.body: Preheat for five minutes. If the butter browns at once, it's too hot.

card.title: Ripping hot, no oil
card.body: The fat renders and seasons the pan for you.

content.quote: By day five my eggs slid like they were on Teflon.
content.author: Maya Reyes

poster.alt: A rusted skillet beside the same skillet restored
poster.name: rust-restore.jpg

card.title: Steel wool, then season
card.body: Scrub to grey metal, rinse, dry over the fire and give it one coat.

card.title: Too much oil
card.body: Bake it off: 45 minutes upside down over high coals, then one thin coat.

card.title: That's on us
card.body: Cracks are covered for life. Send a photo and we'll ship a new one.

value.title: The last ferry to Ilha Grande
value.dek: The island banned cars in 1994. Now a single diesel ferry decides who lives there, and the state wants to replace it.

value.title: Campfire paella for eight
value.dek: One pan, one fire, and the crust everybody fights over.

coverImage.alt: A wide paella pan over a wood fire with lemons on the rim
coverImage.name: campfire-paella.jpg

value.body:
Paella was always outdoor food. In Valencia it's still cooked over orange-wood fires on Sundays, and the socarrat is the point of the whole exercise.1

We cook it on the Cable Fold Grill so the pan sits level over an even bed of coals.

⧉ Product card · component

What you need

Ingredients for eight
IngredientAmount
Bomba rice600 g
Chicken thighs1 kg
Saffron0.5 g2
Stock2.4 L

Don't stir

Once the rice is in, leave it. Stirring releases starch and you'll get risotto.

⧉ Newsletter card · component

footnotes.text: The Valencian regional government registered paella valenciana as a protected cultural asset in 2021.
About 30 threads. Toast them in a dry spoon over the fire before crumbling them in.

value.heading: Why the heat dome stalled over the Pacific Northwest

video.title: Explainer: how a heat dome forms and why it stays put, 3 minutes

poster.alt: A weather map with a red high-pressure dome over Oregon and Washington
poster.name: heat-dome-map.jpg

video.transcript:
Ana Ruiz (climate reporter): In late June, a ridge of high pressure parked over the Northwest. [Wind sounds] Air sinking under that ridge heats up as it's compressed, like a bicycle pump.

Dr. Owen Park (University of Washington): The jet stream bent around it and couldn't push it out for nine days.

image.alt: Line chart of Portland daily highs, June 20 to July 5, peaking at 116°F on June 28
image.name: heat-dome-chart.jpg

figures.longDescription: Daily high temperatures in Portland from June 20 to July 5. Highs sat near 80°F until June 25, climbed each day to a record 116°F on June 28, then fell back below 90°F by July 2. The previous record, 107°F, is marked as a dashed line.
figures.caption: Portland's daily highs, June 20 – July 5.
